text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Companies from South Korea, Taiwan, Japan, Thailand and Vietnam bid on Monday to upgrade four sections of National Highway 1 from Hanoi to the China-border province of Lang Son.
-- The State Bank of Vietnam has said it would intervene to ensure that local commercial banks repay letters of credit to foreign financial institutions if Vietnamese borrowers became insolvent.
-- The State Bank of Vietnam will guarantee the exchange of Vietnamese dong for foreign currency to address reasonable demand of foreign direct investment projects and business cooperation contracts.
-- Malaysian Petronas has formally applied to the Ministry of Planning and Investment to replace Occidental Chemical Corporation in the $70 million project to produce PVC resin in Vietnam.

-- European Commissioner Christos Papoutsis told Deputy Prime Minister Tran Duc Luong that the European Union would be ready to exchange experience with Vietnam and cooperate in developing its energy sector.
-- The State Bank of Vietnam has lowered the ceiling on interest rates for loans made in both dong and the U.S dollar to attract more borrowers.
-- Former Nottingham Forest coach Colin Murphy has been selected as temporary coach for Vietnam's national soccer team from July until October.
-- A press centre of the seventh Francophonie summit, which will be held in Hanoi in November, has been established to provide information and manage media activities during the conference.
-- Ho Chi Minh City's gross domestic product growth was 10.9 percent in the first six months of 1997, below the planned figure of 15 percent.
